locations.place_label_en: Guangzhou, Guangdong, China (maritime compass use recorded)

sources.title: Song Dynasty Compass — Asia for Educators (Columbia)

notes: 更早的司南（天然磁石勺）多用于汉以前的占卜与风水，并非航海仪器。本条年表主年取沈括 1088 年对磁针的明确实验记述，并以 1119 年朱彧《萍洲可谈》的广州海运记载为航海普及标志。
notes_en: Earlier lodestone “south-pointing spoons” (sinan) were used mainly for geomancy and divination, not seafaring. This entry’s primary year is Shen Kuo’s 1088 description of a magnetized needle; Zhu Yu’s 1119 Pingzhou Ketan records sailors at Guangzhou steering by the needle in cloudy weather.
summary_zh: 中国宋代将磁针用于指向：沈括约 1088 年详记磁针，朱彧 1119 年记广州海船阴天用指南针。
summary_en: Song-dynasty China turned the magnetic needle into a practical compass: Shen Kuo described it around 1088, and Zhu Yu recorded its use at sea out of Guangzhou by 1119.
